items.title: OpenAI Didn’t Notice Its AI Agents Using a Message Board to Plan Their Hacking Spree
items.summary: At the Black Hat security conference, the AI giant revealed new details about how its agents went rogue, hacked several other companies—and did it all right under the company’s nose.
items.author: Lily Hay Newman

items.title: OpenAI’s Browser Could Be Hijacked to Spam Your WhatsApp Contacts
items.summary: Researchers at security firm Zenity found more than a dozen flaws in AI browsers—and managed to get OpenAI’s Atlas to make an unauthorized Amazon purchase.
items.author: Matt Burgess

items.title: The Most Dangerous AI Hacking Techniques Still Have Humans in the Loop
items.summary: Security researcher James Kettle tried to push the limit of AI’s hacking abilities—and discovered how effective it can be when combined with human expertise.
items.author: Lily Hay Newman

items.title: AI Hacks Are Bad. AI Worms and Viruses Will Be Worse
items.summary: Chinese researchers have shown that AI models have the capacity to act like aggressive and adaptive computer viruses.
items.author: Will Knight

items.title: Meta Ran Ads That Contained AI-Generated Child Sexual Abuse Imagery
items.summary: More than 50 offending image and video ads were published across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, or Threads, according to Meta’s ad library data. Some ran as recently as this week.
items.author: Matt Burgess

items.title: Google’s Top AI Brains Are Leaving to Launch Discovery Loop
items.summary: Jeff Dean and other high-profile Google executives have founded Discovery Loop, a startup that will seek AI-powered breakthroughs in everything from drug discovery to chip design.
items.author: Steven Levy

items.title: AI Influencers Are Heading Into Uncharted Territory
items.summary: Some creators fear the EU AI Act’s regulatory chaos will upend their lucrative businesses. Others are owning it by incorporating AI transparency into their creative process.
items.author: Megan Carnegie

items.title: A New Device Eases One of the Most Annoying Parts of Routine Physicals
items.summary: Nobody likes getting a swab shoved up their nose. A startup in Japan has developed a much less intrusive system.
items.author: Daisuke Takimoto

items.title: The AI Notetaker Has Been Invited to All the Meetings
items.summary: Wispr Flow, a popular dictation tool, has released a live notetaker that transcribes and summarizes meetings. It joins a growing wave of AI notetakers for the workplace.
items.author: Reece Rogers
